pages.text: The Lens only looks. Once the Chronocortex has grown up a little (stage 1) it can $(o)send$() me: its $(l)Eras$() page lists the times it can reach, but only when I use the $(l)jar itself$() (once it has a body, from the end of the way in). I arrive where I stood, in the land as it was then.

pages.title: The Tether
pages.text: It will not send me without a $(l)Chrono Tether$() (research: Temporal Shift), a pocket watch on a cord of living vein whose other end stays here. Each shift costs Time from its organisms and holds a few minutes; then time snaps me home. Pulling the tether brings me back early. Dying there, I wake at home.

pages.title: Where It Can Send Me
pages.text: $(l)The Age of the Precursors$(): before the villagers, a taller people built cities of gold and stone. Every ruin I know was new then. Their cities are alive.$(br2)$(l)The Ice Age$(): the same hills under ice. It must be taught $(l)the cold$() (blue ice) and remember the Precursors first.$(br2)Shifting is hard on an unprotected body.

pages.title: Time Capsules
pages.text: It cannot reach past the Ice Age on its own. A $(l)Time Capsule$() built into its last shell, in place of a frame, lets it reach the $(l)Jurassic$(); a second, the $(l)Hadean$() and what is before.$(br2)The first I must piece together: a $(l)casing$() from the Precursors' vaults and tombs, an $(l)escapement$() from their archives, a $(l)heart$() from the Ice Age's temple remains and a $(l)seal$() its beasts carry, with two sunbrass. The second stands at the heart of every Jurassic temple, held still with the rest of it.

pages.title: What Lasts
pages.text: What I build in another era is still there when I come home, if it is made to last: stone, deepslate, sandstone, prismarine, brick, terracotta, gold, copper, amethyst. It has stood all the ages between, so I find it crumbled (cracked, mossed, worn, green with verdigris; gold just as it was), and the Lens sees it too.$(br2)Wood, glass and wool rot away. What I break again before I leave never stood at all.

pages.title: Held
pages.text: Warded head to foot, an era holds me for as long as I please. Only the tether takes me home (or taking a piece of the suit off: then it begins to let go).

pages.title: The Ice Age
pages.text: The temples' stones still stand in the ice, broken, and the obelisk whole among them. Where the core hung, its last moment froze round it: Aeon Ice. Nothing moves in it. A block of it against a Time organism steadies it more than any Density.$(br2)Mammoths walk the slopes in herds; woolly rhinoceroses charge; a pale cat with sabre teeth hunts anything that walks upright.
